You have a monorepo (mesh) containing another monorepo (ranch) that holds
the UI for everything plus the backend components serving the ranch's
agents. Over time, components were renamed, aliased, duplicated, and
scattered. Your job is to read the code, decide the correct shape, then
apply it: name everything correctly, merge duplicates, move components
into their monorepos, eliminate retired names, remove all symlinks, and
verify the running system.

The code is the truth. Directory names are not evidence. Read before
deciding.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

mesh is a monorepo. ranch is one of its children. ranch is itself a
monorepo holding the UI for everything plus backend components.

Known children of ranch, after this plan's renames:
  stockyard/       (was routers/) — the chute that sorts and dispatches
                    stock. Holds herd and flock.
  barn/            (was mcp/) — the compartment for every tool the
                    operation uses, ours and third-party.
  corral/          role unknown — read its code.
  paddock/         role unknown — read its code.
  ui/              the UI for everything.

Known children of stockyard: herd (router), flock (free-pool provider).
Known child of barn: shep.
Known child of mesh, sibling of ranch: squawk.

The router codebase appears under three names: herd, llama-swap,
sovereign-swap. One codebase. Canonical name is herd. Retired names are
eliminated from paths, symlinks, service names, and tasks. The binary
inside herd may keep the filename llama-swap only if an external
consumer requires that exact name; read the Makefile, deploy scripts,
and the running process's argv[0] to decide.

super-ralph is not ranch. Find its code and determine what it actually
is. It may be an alias, a distinct component, or something else.

Folder names that describe mechanism instead of role are replaced:
  routers → stockyard
  mcp     → barn

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
HOW TO DECIDE WHAT A THING IS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For every candidate directory, answer these from evidence only:

  What is the module identity?
    go     grep '^module ' go.mod
    node   jq -r .name package.json
    rust   grep '^name = ' Cargo.toml
    py     grep '^name = ' pyproject.toml
    none   "no manifest — container or unknown"

  What is the entrypoint?  (main.go, index.ts, server.go)
  What does it expose?     (HTTP routes, CLI verbs, MCP tools)
  What does it import?     (from go.mod / package.json / imports)
  What imports it?         (rg its module path across siblings)
  Is it running?           (pgrep, /proc/$pid/exe, /proc/$pid/cwd)
  Where does config point? (pitchfork.toml, mise.toml, systemd units)

Two directories with the same module identity are the same codebase.
That is the definition of a duplicate. Names are irrelevant.

Classify each candidate as exactly one:

  monorepo             has 2+ children each with a distinct module path
  child-component      one manifest, one entrypoint
  retired-alias        same module identity as another; merge to survivor
  duplicate-checkout   same module identity, different HEAD; merge by hand
  container-wrapper    no manifest, only holds other projects; collapse
  symlink              resolves elsewhere; delete after updating callers
  unknown              evidence thin; read one more file, then decide

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
ORDER OF OPERATIONS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Do not move, rename, or delete anything until you have identified every
duplicate by module identity. Merging comes first — always. Moving first
breaks history and hides duplicates.

  1. Inventory by module identity. Bounded scans only. Never glob
     ~/sovereign root. Use fd with max-depth and specific paths.

  2. Classify every candidate per the rules above.

  3. Merge every module-identity group with 2+ members, per-file, by
     hand, using the merge procedure below. Survivor chosen by:
     metaphor fit, else most recent commit, else live process, else
     cleanliness.

  4. Rename folders: routers → stockyard, mcp → barn (git mv inside the
     containing repo).

  5. Move child-components into their monorepos (git mv). Rename
     retired-alias directories to their canonical names. Rename the
     binary only if nothing external depends on the old filename.

  6. Update every reference in pitchfork.toml, mise.toml, stack/services,
     systemd units, environment.d, launchers, .gitmodules, and
     ~/.bashrc.env. Never touch ~/.bashrc.

  7. Delete every user-created symlink after updating its callers to
     the canonical path. Repeat until fd -t l returns zero.

  8. Build, test, restart, health-check, model-count. Assert no
     symlinks, no retired names, no conflict markers.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
MERGE PROCEDURE (per duplicate group, per file)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Before touching: git update-ref refs/recovery/pre-merge HEAD on every
side of the group.

  base=$(git -C <A> merge-base HEAD <B-HEAD>)
  If merge-base fails, the pair is unrelated — not a merge. Note it and
  move on.

  git -C <survivor> worktree add --detach \
      ~/.recovery-worktrees/merge-<name> <older-HEAD>
  git -C ~/.recovery-worktrees/merge-<name> merge --no-commit --no-ff \
      <newer-HEAD>

  For every conflicted file:
    git show :1:<file> > /tmp/base
    git show :2:<file> > /tmp/ours
    git show :3:<file> > /tmp/theirs
    Read all three. Write the file that should exist.

    take-a      the other side was superseded, broken, or redundant
    take-b      this side was superseded, broken, or redundant
    merge       both sides added independent code; combine by hand
    hand-write  both sides edited the same logic; write the correct
                version. Do not concatenate. Do not blend.

  Forbidden forever: -X ours, -X theirs, --ours, --theirs, --union,
  git merge-file, or any conflict marker in committed output.

  Write MERGE-DECISIONS.md at the survivor root, one entry per
  non-trivial file:
    path:
    ours:    what side A changed and why
    theirs:  what side B changed and why
    decision: take-a | take-b | merge | hand-write
    reason:  one sentence citing specific commits

  Commit. Fast-forward survivor.

  For every other member of the group:
    tar czf ~/.recovery-archive/<ts>/<basename>.tar.gz <loser>/
    rm -rf <loser>
    rg the tree for the loser path; update every hit to survivor path.
    Any symlink pointing at the loser: delete after updating callers.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
CONFIG REWRITE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For every retired string, rg across ~/sovereign, ~/projects, ~/.config,
~/.local/bin, ~/.agent:

  super-ralph
  llama-swap       (as a path or service name; not as an argv[0] if
                    externally required)
  sovereign-swap
  ranch/routers
  ranch/mcp

Zero hits, or the remaining hit has an inline comment
"# required by <external thing>, do not rename" on the same line.

Config files that must be updated when their path references change:
  ~/sovereign/pitchfork.toml
  ~/sovereign/mise.toml
  ~/sovereign/stack/services/*.sh
  ~/sovereign/config/*
  ~/sovereign/.gitmodules
  ~/.config/systemd/user/*.service
  ~/.config/systemd/user/*.path
  ~/.config/systemd/user/*.socket
  ~/.config/environment.d/*
  ~/.local/bin/* launchers
  ~/.bashrc.env (symlink into a tracked file — commit if you edit)

Never edit ~/.bashrc.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
SYMLINK PURGE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Final state has zero user-created symlinks under ~/sovereign and
~/projects. OS-managed symlinks under /usr/lib/systemd/user/*.wants are
out of scope.

For every symlink:
  readlink -f it.
  If target is canonical and survives: update every reference to the
  symlink path so it points at the canonical path directly, then delete
  the symlink.
  If target is archived: delete the symlink, update callers to survivor.
  Loop until fd -t l returns zero.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
VERIFY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For each Go module touched: go build ./... && go test ./... && go vet ./...
For each other language module: run its equivalent.

  ./<router-binary> --validate -config ~/sovereign/config/herd.yaml
  mise -C ~/sovereign run restart-herd
  curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:25100/health
  curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:25100/v1/models | jq '.data | length'

Assertions, all must be zero:
  fd -t l -H . ~/sovereign ~/projects | wc -l
  rg -c 'super-ralph|llama-swap|sovereign-swap' \
     ~/sovereign ~/projects 2>/dev/null | wc -l
  rg -c '^<<<<<<<|^=======|^>>>>>>>' \
     ~/sovereign ~/projects 2>/dev/null | wc -l

If any assertion fails, fix the cause and re-run. Do not report success
until all three hold.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
RULES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Read before naming. The code is truth.
Merge duplicates before moving.
No mechanical conflict resolution.
No symlinks at the end.
No retired names in paths or configs.
No conflict markers in committed files.
No progress reports. No mid-task summaries.
No asking which name is correct — read the code, decide, do it.
Never reset --hard. Never clean -fdx. Never rm -rf without archiving.
Never edit ~/.bashrc.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
FINAL OUTPUT — exactly this, nothing else
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

  mesh/
    ranch     <path>  <role>
    squawk    <path>  <role>
    <other>   <path>  <role>

  mesh/ranch/
    stockyard:
      herd    <path>  <HEAD>  <module>
      flock   <path>  <HEAD>  <module>
    barn:
      shep    <path>  <HEAD>  <module>
      <other> <path>  <HEAD>  <module>
    corral    <path>  <HEAD>  <role from code>
    paddock   <path>  <HEAD>  <role from code>
    ui        <path>  <HEAD>
    <other>   <path>  <HEAD>  <role from code>

  super-ralph (resolved):
    identity:    <what the code says it is>
    disposition: kept | merged into <survivor> @ <sha> | archived

  mergers:
    <A> + <B> → <survivor>  merge-sha <sha>  MERGE-DECISIONS.md <path>

  moved:    <old> → <new>
  renamed:  <old> → <new>
  archived: <count> under ~/.recovery-archive/<ts>/

  symlinks in tree:      0
  retired names in tree: 0
  conflict markers:      0

  build:  pass | fail
  test:   pass | fail
  health: <curl body>
  models: <number>

Begin with step 1. Read the code. Do not ask.
</attachment>
